definitions.explanation: An injury that is severe and requires significant medical treatment. In Japanese legal and medical contexts, generally defined as an injury requiring more than 30 days of treatment.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}で{重傷|じゅうしょう}を{負|お}った。
examples.english: He sustained serious injuries in the accident.

examples.japanese: {重傷|じゅうしょう}{者|しゃ}は{病院|びょういん}に{搬送|はんそう}された。
examples.english: The seriously injured were transported to the hospital.

examples.japanese: {幸|さいわ}い{命|いのち}に{別状|べつじょう}はなかったが、{足|あし}に{重傷|じゅうしょう}を{負|お}い、{入院|にゅういん}することになった。
examples.english: Fortunately his life was not in danger, but he sustained a serious leg injury and had to be hospitalized.

notes:
{重傷|じゅうしょう} refers to physical injuries. It is commonly seen in news reports about accidents, crimes, and disasters.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {重傷|じゅうしょう}を{負|お}う (to sustain serious injuries)
- {重傷|じゅうしょう}{者|しゃ} (seriously injured person)
- {全治|ぜんち}〇{週間|しゅうかん}の{重傷|じゅうしょう} (serious injury requiring X weeks to heal)

Distinct from {重症|じゅうしょう} (serious illness/condition), which is a homophone. {重傷|じゅうしょう} uses the kanji {傷|しょう} (wound/injury) and refers to physical wounds, while {重症|じゅうしょう} uses {症|しょう} (condition/symptom) and refers to a severe state of illness. The opposite is {軽傷|けいしょう} (minor injury).
